title: India Inc’s Earnings Rebound Faces Commodity Cost Headwinds

faq.q: What are "commodity costs" in this context?
faq.a: Commodity costs refer to the prices of basic raw materials and inputs that companies use in their production processes, such as crude oil, natural gas, various metals (steel, aluminium), chemicals, agricultural produce, and even freight charges for transportation.

faq.q: How do rising commodity costs affect corporate earnings?
faq.a: When commodity costs rise, a company's cost of goods sold (COGS) increases. If the company cannot fully pass on these higher costs to consumers through price hikes, its gross profit margins and, subsequently, its net profits will shrink.

faq.q: Which sectors are most affected by rising commodity prices?
faq.a: Sectors that are highly dependent on raw material inputs, such as manufacturing (automobiles, cement, consumer durables), chemicals, and those with limited pricing power, are generally most impacted. Oil marketing companies are also sensitive to crude oil price fluctuations.

faq.q: What is "pricing power" and why is it important?
faq.a: Pricing power is a company's ability to raise its product or service prices without significantly losing customer demand or market share. Companies with strong brands, unique products, or essential offerings tend to have greater pricing power, allowing them to better offset rising input costs.

Q2 FY27 refers to the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27. In India, the financial year runs from April 1 to March 31, so Q2 covers the period from July 1 to September 30, 2026.
